Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the run chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Ravichandran Ashwin has still not arrived at the ground, and Devdutt Padikkal is the substitute fielder in place of him. Zak Crawley and Ben Duckett are the two openers for England. Jasprit Bumrah has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Here we go...
... FOURTH INNINGS ...

Brilliant batting performance by the Indian batters. They have completely batted England out of the game. Yashasvi Jaiswal has taken to international cricket like a fish to water and scored another 214 not out in the second innings of the match. With shots all around the ground and hitting 12 sixes in a Test inning, Yashasvi Jaiswal has provided a batting treat for the viewers. Shubman Gill again stood up and got 91 in the second innings of a Test match, giving India the platform for a launch. Then the pair of Yashasvi Jaiswal and Sarfaraz Khan took the final attack on the English bowlers and got their side to 430 runs before Rohit Sharma thought there was enough time left in this Test match to bowl England out. England now faces the challenge of chasing down 557 runs.

India has put up a mammoth lead of 556 runs in front of England to chase down in their final innings. Yashasvi Jaiswal comes out unbeaten on 214 runs along with the debutant Sarfaraz Khan who too batted brilliantly for his 68 not out. India declares on 430/4 after batting for 98 overs.

Short and outside off, Sarfaraz Khan guides it towards point for a single. 18 runs off the over. Rohit Sharma is waving his hands and India have declared on 430/4. So, the target for England will be a massive 557!

England have been on the back foot since morning. They have not gotten many chances since morning and have converted the ones that came their way. Getting Shubman Gill was a huge bonus for them but since then, they have been pushed further back. Ben Stokes and England are waiting for a declaration from India as they walk out for Lunch. Every single run scored from here on is a burden for England. The lead is already 440 runs. How many more runs would India pile on before Rohit Sharma decides to declare? Let's find out after LUNCH on Day 4. Stay tuned as we will be back at 12.10 pm IST (6.40 am GMT).

India started the Day with Shubman Gill and Kuldeep Yadav who both went on to put up a partnership of 50+ before Shubman Gill got run out at 91. Yashasvi Jaiswal who went back retired hurt yesterday, came out to bat at 123. Kuldeep was dismissed soon after and that got in the debutant Sarfaraz Khan. Both Yashasvi and Sarfaraz batted beautifully and started hitting some brilliant shots around the ground, putting up another 50+ partnership and are still at the crease.

SESSION SUMMARY- 31 OVERS, 118 RUNS, 2 WICKETS. That brings us to the end of the First Session on Day 4 of this Test Match between India and England. India sits on a huge lead of 440 runs and is 314/4 in their second innings with Yashasvi Jaiswal batting on 149 and Sarfaraz Khan on 22 at the crease. Although the wicket of Shubman Gill on 91 came as a heartbreak for the Indian fans, their position in the game is certainly very strong and it's getting better with every run scored.

Ashwin's pivotal role in spearheading India's bowling attack on Day 2, where he claimed his 500th Test wicket by dismissing Zak Crawley, highlights the challenge that India will face in his absence. Yet, with Mohammed Siraj also making crucial breakthroughs, the Indian bowling unit will be eager to capitalize on their momentum and maintain their stranglehold over the English batters. As the match enters a crucial phase, both teams will be looking to seize the initiative and gain the upper hand in what promises to be an exhilarating day of cricket.

The heroics of Yashasvi Jaiswal in the final session of Day 3 turned the tide firmly in India's favor, with his magnificent century taking the game away from England and putting the hosts in a dominant position. Jaiswal's sublime batting display has left the visitors reeling, and India will be hoping for more of the same from their batters as they look to consolidate their position of strength.

As the sun rises on Day 4 of this gripping Test match between India and England, the stage is set for another day of enthralling cricketing action. Mohammed Siraj is up for a quick chat. He talks about the plans being very well executed at the field from the start and that's what set the tone for him to grab those quick wickets. He adds by saying that a yorker is a very good option to bowl in a Test match and get a lot of wickets. He talks about being consistent with the line and lengths which is very important against these English batters. Ends by saying that the rest was really good for him and helped him come back well.

After Tea, the two young Indian batters showcased their class. Initially, they focused on rotating the strike and respecting good deliveries. However, once Yashasvi Jaiswal reached his half-century, he shifted gears and Shubman Gill also began to play his shots freely. Jaiswal's wide array of strokes was evident as he aggressively tackled the English bowlers, achieving a splendid century, his second of the series. Gill played a supportive role, securing his own fifty as well. Unfortunately, while celebrating his hundred, Jaiswal sustained a back injury and had to retire hurt. Rajat Patidar failed to make an impact, departing for a duck. Gill remained solid at the crease and, along with nightwatchman Kuldeep Yadav, played out till Stumps, extending the hosts' lead to a massive 322 runs.

The second session clearly belonged to India, as Ben Stokes' dismissal while attempting to accelerate, followed by Ben Foakes' quick departure on the next ball, shifted the momentum decisively in favor of the hosts. Despite Ben Duckett's exceptional century, England suffered a collapse after being 207/2 and were eventually bowled out for 319 runs. Ravindra Jadeja made crucial breakthroughs after Lunch, dismissing the English skipper among others, while Mohammed Siraj swiftly wrapped up the innings. In response, India's openers adopted a cautious approach, aiming to tire out the English bowlers. However, skipper Rohit Sharma fell to Joe Root's bowling just before Tea. Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill ensured no further setbacks, guiding India to a lead of 170 runs by the end of the session.

England began their batting innings with the scoreboard showing 207/2, with Ben Duckett batting at 133 and Root providing support. However, Joe Root's decision to attempt his favorite reverse scoop resulted in his dismissal, a pivotal moment in the game. Jonny Bairstow followed suit, falling for a duck to a brilliant delivery from Kuldeep Yadav. The loss of early wickets forced Duckett to alter his approach, ultimately leading to his downfall after a superb knock of 153 runs. Skipper Ben Stokes anchored one end firmly and unleashed some powerful shots towards the end of the session, while Ben Foakes initially struggled but managed to survive until Lunch. The Indian bowlers were relentless from the start, with Jasprit Bumrah setting the tone by dismissing Root, and Kuldeep weaving a spell around the English batters, giving the hosts a slight advantage heading into the break.

India concludes Day 3 with a significant advantage in this Test match. Session Summary - 152 runs and 1 wicket in 35 overs. Termed the 'Moving Day', the game has distinctly shifted in favor of the hosts. Despite concerns over the absence of Ravichandran Ashwin, the Indian bowlers showcased remarkable resilience, staging a fine fightback. Their stellar bowling performance provided the platform for the batters to express themselves freely. Yashasvi Jaiswal capitalized on this opportunity, crafting a splendid century, while Shubman Gill redeemed himself after a lackluster first innings. Their performances have propelled the Men in Blue into a commanding position in the match.

SESSION SUMMARY - 73 runs and 6 wickets in 26.1 overs. India's session by a mile! England were in a decent position after Lunch, but Ben Stokes got a bit greedy and lost his wicket in the process. The very next ball, Ben Foakes went back to the hut that put the visitors on the back foot again. The tail couldn't wag around for much and they conceded a lead of 126 runs which was disappointing as at one point they were looking likely to get much closer to the Indian total. Ravindra Jadeja got the big wicket of the opposition skipper and added another to his tally later on while Mohammed Siraj cleaned up the tail quickly and ended up with a four-wicket hall. The Indian openers got off to a steady start as run scoring wasn't that easy with the English bowlers hitting the right line and lengths. However, the skipper Rohit Sharma fell victim to Joe Root not too long before Tea, and Yashasvi Jaiswal and Shubman Gill had to be cautious and saw out till the end of the session as the hosts went into the break with a lead of 170 runs. The hosts would like to extend this further while England hopes to pick up a few wickets in the next session to restrict India from posting a big target.
